column1: # Pairs of consecutive onset charts between which the source redrew bars
# What an entry asserts. Between these two charts the source lowered the bars
# of settled onset dates and kept them lower in every later chart: cases were
# withdrawn from those dates, not misread by us. The evidence is the chart's
# own printed total (`n = ...` in its title), which is independent of our
# reader, and the bars read against the image.
# What it does. `build_reporting_delay.py` counts a fall between the named
# charts as `n_withdrawn_by_source` and resets each fallen bar's highest
# reading to its new height, so growth after the redraw counts as arrivals
# again. A fall between any other pair is a dip: it is recorded as
# `n_dip_ignored` and changes nothing else. Without an entry here a real
# withdrawal would hold back every later arrival on the same onset date
# until the bar passed its old height.
# An entry must name two charts that are consecutive among the accepted ones.
# If the reader later accepts a chart between them the build stops, and the
# entry is rewritten against the pair the falls then sit in.
# `verified_by` says who read the bars against the image and when.
